questions.question: At the top price, Vaibhav Vyapaar Limited's P/E is 44.3x. Similar listed companies have a P/E of about 25.2x. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It costs about the same as, or less than, similar companies for each rupee of profit.
It costs more than similar companies for each rupee of profit, so its profit must grow faster to be worth it.
The P/E shows how many shares the company has.

questions.explanation: A P/E of 44.3x against 25.2x means you pay far more for each rupee of Vaibhav Vyapaar Limited's profit than for its peers'. Its profit would need to grow much faster for that to pay off.

questions.question: Sales went from ₹25.25 crore in FY24 to ₹36.80 crore in FY26, which is 20.7% a year. How would you describe that?
questions.explanation: 20.7% a year is healthy growth: Vaibhav Vyapaar Limited's customers are buying more each year.

questions.question: Vaibhav Vyapaar Limited owes 1.6 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 1.6 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, lenders have more riding on Vaibhav Vyapaar Limited than its owners, and repayments are due even in bad years.
